name: layout.ring
doc: Nodes evenly around a ring, so that a cycle of edges is drawn as the rim rather than as chords across it. The nodes are seated in the order of a depth-first walk of the edges read as undirected, from the first node in input order, each node's neighbours tried earliest in input order first, an edge from a node to itself and an edge to a node not in the input ignored, and the walk continuing from the earliest node not yet seated when a component is exhausted. With n nodes, the i-th seated node's centre is at angle 2πi/n − π/2 from the positive x axis, so the first is at the top and the rest follow clockwise in the canvas's coordinates (y downward), at the radius max(s, n·s/2π), where s is the widest node's width plus `separation`. A node's top-left corner is its centre less half its width and half its height, each coordinate rounded to six decimals with ties to even and never a negative zero. A single node stands with its top-left corner at (0, 0); an input without nodes places none. Every node is placed; pins are not consulted.

separation.doc: The clear space kept between neighbours on the ring, added to the widest node's width to give the arc each node is seated on.
